### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace executed exactly one of four activities between A37 and A22: A14 in about 27 in 100 cases, A15 in about 25, A20 in about 23 and A21 in about 25, and no trace contained more than one of the four [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL001, REL010].
- These four activities always sat in that slot: A37 preceded each of them and each preceded A22 in every trace where they occurred, and the only observed outgoing transitions of A20 and A21 led to A22 [REL004, REL005, REL008, REL009, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR001, DIR002].
- In the later window, this intermediate step has almost disappeared: A20 and A21 appear in none of the 200 traces, A14 in 2 traces (about 1 in 100) and A15 in 1 trace (about 0.5 in 100) [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004].
- Routing out of A37 changed accordingly: its outgoing transitions, previously split almost evenly across A14, A15, A20 and A21 (23–27% each), now go to A22 in about 98.5 in 100 cases, with only about 1 in 100 to A14 and 0.5 in 100 to A15 [DIR003].
- The distance from A37 to A22 shrank from consistently 2 event positions (all 200 traces) to 1 position in about 197 of 200 traces, i.e. A22 now immediately follows A37 [LAG001].
- A22 itself is unchanged in participation (present in every trace in both windows); its mean relative position moved only slightly earlier, from about 0.39 to about 0.38 of the trace [POS005].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the intermediate step between A37 and A22 — previously an exclusive choice of one of A14, A15, A20 or A21 in roughly equal shares — is skipped in almost all cases, so that A37 is followed directly by A22. The support is direct and consistent across indicator types: A37's outgoing transitions rerouted to A22, the A37-to-A22 distance collapsed from two positions to one, co-occurrence of each of the four activities with A22 fell from about 23–27 in 100 cases to about 0–1, and participation of the four activities fell to zero or near zero [DIR003, LAG001, REL004, REL008, REL011, REL013, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]. The volume of evidence (27 items against roughly 0.38 expected by chance in an unchanged process) makes a chance explanation of the pattern as a whole implausible, and each individual difference is also larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data.

Limitations remain: the items are not independent, since most restate the same underlying trace behaviour, and the two windows are finite samples in which variant frequencies can differ without any change. The evidence also cannot distinguish a removed branch from one whose execution probability dropped sharply — the later window still shows the old behaviour in about 1–2 in 100 cases (A14 twice, A15 once), and the absence of A20 and A21 only means they were not observed, not that they have left the process [OCC003, OCC004, DIR003].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 76 units tested, 0.38 items expected without change.
- Evidence items: 26 items total (OCC001-004, DIR001-003, POS001-005, REL001-014, LAG001).

First step per instructions: compare number of evidence items with items_expected_without_change. 26 items vs 0.38 expected — that's many times larger (about 68x). So the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we don't go to "Insufficient evidence" on the count basis. Then judge by directness, consistency, ability to rule out competing explanations.

Now, what's the behavioural story?

Before window:
- A14: participation 0.27 (54/200 traces), mean occurrences 0.27.
- A15: participation 0.25 (50/200).
- A20: participation 0.23 (46/200).
- A21: participation 0.25 (50/200).
- A22: participation 1.0 (all 200 traces), mean position ~0.394 of trace.
- A37: DIR003 shows A37's outgoing transitions: before, A37 → A20 (0.23), A15 (0.25), A14 (0.27), A21 (0.25). These shares sum to 1.0. So A37 is followed by one of {A14, A15, A20, A21} — a choice among four alternatives, roughly uniform (23-27% each).

After window:
- A14: participation 0.01 (2/200).
- A15: participation 0.005 (1/200).
- A20: participation 0.0 (0/200).
- A21: participation 0.0 (0/200).
- A22: participation 1.0, mean position ~0.378 (slightly earlier).
- A37's outgoing: A22 0.985, A14 0.01, A15 0.005. So after, A37 is almost always followed by A22.

LAG001: pair (A37, A22): before, the gap between A37 and A22 was 2 steps in 100% of cases; after, gap 1 step in 98.5% of cases. So A22 now immediately follows A37 (within 1 step), whereas before it was 2 steps after.

REL items with A22: before, A14 co-occurred with A22 in 27% of traces with A14 before A22 (A_before_B 0.27); after, co-occurrence 0.01. Similarly for A15, A20, A21. So before, when A14/A15/A20/A21 occurred, they occurred between A37 and A22 (A37 → X → A22, gap 2). After, they're gone and A37 → A22 directly (gap 1).

So the picture: before, in roughly a quarter of cases each, one of four activities (A14, A15, A20, A21) was executed between A37 and A22 — apparently a choice of one of four mutually exclusive activities (since co-occurrence among them is 0: REL001 shows A14 & A15 co-occurrence 0.0, A_only 0.27, B_only 0.25, neither 0.48 — so they never co-occur; each trace contains at most one of them). After, this intermediate step is almost entirely skipped: A37 is directly followed by A22.

Wait — but is A22 always after A37? REL004: A14 & A22: before co-occurrence 0.27, A_before_B 0.27 (A14 before A22). B_only 0.73 — A22 without A14 in 73% of traces. So A22 occurs in all traces; A14 occurs in 27% and always before A22. LAG001 (A37, A22): before gap 2 always; after gap 1 in 98.5%.

So the structural hypothesis: the optional intermediate activity (one of A14/A15/A20/A21, chosen exclusively) between A37 and A22 was removed/skipped in the later window — i.e., the branch from A37 to {A14,A15,A20,A21} was essentially eliminated, with A37 now flowing directly to A22.

Is this "order/placement" hypothesis needing relational evidence? The hypothesis here is more like "part of the process is executed less often / skipped". That's participation/routing evidence: OCC (participation dropped to ~0), DIR (A37's outgoing redistributed from the four activities to A22), REL (co-occurrence of each of the four with A22 dropped), LAG (gap between A37 and A22 changed from 2 to 1). These directly support "the intermediate step between A37 and A22 is skipped".

Actually the LAG change from 2 to 1 is direct relational/positional evidence that A22 now immediately follows A37. And DIR003 shows A37's successor distribution changed. So the hypothesis "the four-way choice of intermediate activity after A37 was dropped, so A37 now leads directly to A22" is supported directly and consistently.

Competing explanations: sampling differences in variant frequencies — the four activities each appeared in ~25% of traces before; could the after-window just be a sample where this variant didn't appear? With 200 traces and each at ~25%, all four dropping to 0-1% simultaneously is extremely unlikely under stable process (empirical strength 0.995 for each, though these items are not independent — they reflect the same underlying behaviour). But the consistency across indicators and the LAG shift from 2 to 1 makes a pure sampling explanation implausible. Still, we should mention that the windows are finite samples and variant frequencies can differ; also the after-window still shows residual occurrences (A14 in 2 traces, A15 in 1 trace), so the branch isn't completely gone — it's executed in about 1-2% of cases.

Also note: A22's position shifted slightly earlier (mean relative position 0.394 → 0.378), consistent with removing an intermediate step.

Number of items: 26 vs 0.38 expected — many times larger. Good.

Now, is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence is direct (DIR, LAG, REL, OCC all consistent), the count is far beyond chance, and the competing explanation (sampling) is made implausible by the magnitude and consistency. State it as a possibility supported by the evidence, not as a confirmed modification, with its supporting signs and limitations."

I think Supported hypothesis is right. The hypothesis: in the later window, the optional step following A37 — previously one of A14, A15, A20, A21 (mutually exclusive, each in roughly a quarter of cases) — is almost always skipped, so A37 is directly followed by A22.

Let me double check the mutual exclusivity: REL001 (A14,A15): before co-occurrence 0.0, A_only 0.27, B_only 0.25, neither 0.48. Sum: 0.27+0.25+0.48 = 1.0. So A14 and A15 never co-occur. REL002 (A14,A20): co-occurrence 0.0. REL010 (A20,A21): co-occurrence 0.0. So yes, the four are mutually exclusive. Each trace contains at most one of them, and 52% of traces contain none (before). After, ~99% contain none.

Also check: before, does every trace with one of the four have it between A37 and A22? DIR001: A20's outgoing transitions: A22 1.0 — all observed outgoing transitions of A20 go to A22. DIR002: A21 → A22 1.0. We don't have DIR for A14/A15 but REL004/REL005 show A14 before A22 (A_before_B 0.27) and A14 before A37? REL005 (A14, A37): B_before_A 0.27 — A37 before A14. So A37 → A14 → A22. Similarly REL009 (A15, A37): B_before_A 0.25 — A37 before A15; REL008 (A15, A22): A_before_B 0.25 — A15 before A22. So yes: A37 → {A14|A15|A20|A21} → A22.

LAG001 confirms: A37 to A22 gap of 2 before (one activity in between), gap 1 after (direct).

After window: DIR003: A37 → A22 0.985, A37 → A14 0.01, A37 → A15 0.005. So in ~2% of traces the old branch persists (A14 in 2 traces, A15 in 1 trace). A20 and A21 not observed at all after.

So the behavioural description:

- Before, about 1 in 4 traces each contained one of A14, A15, A20, A21 (participation 27%, 25%, 23%, 25%), always exactly one, never more, and always between A37 and A22.
- In the later window, these activities nearly vanish: A20 and A21 not observed at all (0 of 200 traces), A14 in about 1 in 100 (2/200), A15 in about 0.5 in 100 (1/200).
- A37's outgoing transitions changed: before split roughly evenly among A14 (27%), A15 (25%), A20 (23%), A21 (25%); after, 98.5% go to A22, with tiny residuals to A14 (1%) and A15 (0.5%).
- The A37→A22 distance changed from consistently 2 steps to 1 step in ~98.5% of cases.
- Co-occurrence of each of the four with A22 dropped from ~23-27% to ~0-1%.
- A22 still occurs in every trace; its relative position moved slightly earlier (mean ~0.39 → ~0.38).

All items have empirical_strength 0.995, but note they largely reflect one underlying behaviour; the count comparison (26 items vs 0.38 expected) is what establishes this isn't chance.

Support level: Supported hypothesis.

Hypothesis: In the later window, the branch in which one of A14/A15/A20/A21 executes between A37 and A22 is almost always skipped; A37 flows directly to A22. This is a "part of the process executed less often / skipped" hypothesis, supported by participation (OCC), routing (DIR), relational (REL), and lag (LAG) evidence, all consistent.

Limitations / competing explanations: finite samples — variant frequencies can differ between windows; a stable process with a ~25%-each four-way variant would virtually never show all four at 0-1% in 200 traces, but the residual occurrences (3 traces) show the branch isn't strictly removed. Also, we cannot tell whether the activities were removed from the model or the choice probability dropped to near zero; zero participation only means not observed. Also, several indicators reflect the same trace behaviour, so they're not independent confirmations.
